newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: EU seeks info on Bank Austria bid for CA.
newsitem.headline: EU seeks info on Bank Austria bid for CA.

text.p: The European Commission has written to Austria for details of Bank Austria's bid for its rival Creditanstalt-Bankverein, the finance ministry said on Friday.

It confirmed media reports that EU authorities were particularly interested in guarantees provided for Bank Austria by the City of Vienna and the state's double role as Creditanstalt seller and potential buyer.
The state controls 20 percent of Bank Austria voting stock, or around 17 percent of total equity.
"According to our understanding, this is purely a routine matter," a finance ministry spokesman said.

Market leader Bank Austria is thought to be the highest of three bidders for the state's 70 percent of ordinary voting shares in Creditanstalt. But the offer, reportedly worth some 16 billion schillings ($1.5 billion), has sparked a domestic political row.

Conservatives say a sale to Bank Austria would not be a genuine privatisation because the bank is effectively controlled by the City of Vienna through its foundation Anteilsverwaltung Zentralsparkasse (AVZ).

AVZ directly owns around 46 percent of Bank Austria voting shares, or 40 percent of total equity, and indirectly controls a majority. It also guarantees Bank Austria's liabilities, ensuring it an AAA credit rating.
The AVZ and Bank Austria supervisory boards are very similar and Bank Austria chief executive Gerhard Randa sits on both.

The European Commission is also seeking information on a 10-year transition period granted to Bank Austria to bring its accounting into line with EU directives and it has asked how Bank Austria plans to finance the deal, according to press reports.
The European Union wants a reply from the Austrian government by mid January. -- Janet McBride, Vienna Newsroom, 43-1-53112-254 ($ = 10.93 Austrian Schillings)
